title: Burst reserve alignment and role-swap scenarios (Fall 2026)
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet explores how to align reserved capacity (monthly committed GPU hours) with burst capacity and headcount decisions via a role-swapbook approach. Goal is to quantify tradeoffs across three pricing sensitivity pivots and recommended hiring/contractor mixes to preserve margin while maintaining throughput SLAs.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
We model three scenarios (Base / Conservative / Aggressive) for Q4'26–Q2'27 that combine token demand trajectories, reserved vs burst capacity mixes, and a role-swapbook where hiring choices (senior IC vs two juniors + contractor) shift fixed vs variable cost. Under moderate token price compression (-10%) the swapbook reduces fixed monthly cost by ~8% with a 3–5% throughput regression but preserves gross margin better than straight hiring freezes. Recommended immediate action: implement a small pilot (one squad) using swapbook hires + increased burst budget capped at 20% of peak capacity; set pricing trigger rules to push to a 15% reserved cut if sustained token price drop >12% for 6 weeks.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Model horizon: 6 quarters (Q4'26–Q1'28).
- Baseline token demand growth: +22% Q/Q for Q4'26 then normalizing to +8% Q/Q thereafter in Base.
- Reserved GPU cost: $0.95 / GPU-hour (committed), burst GPU cost: $2.70 / GPU-hour (on-demand + infra overhead).
- Avg tokens per request and per-GPU throughput derived from serving-runtime baseline (seq avg=320 tokens, 120 seq/sec per A100-equivalent while batched).
- Hiring fully loaded cost for Senior Infra (L5 equivalent): $36k/mo; Junior (L3): $11k/mo; Contractor (ML infra/ops) blended: $18k/mo for project work.
- Quality/regression risk of swapbook: estimated 3–7% increased token cost (more retries, tuning) in first 8 weeks.

Scenario summary table (text):
| Scenario     | Demand growth Q1 | Reserved % of peak | Monthly reserved cost | Monthly burst cost | New hires (FTE) | Contractors |
|--------------|------------------|--------------------|-----------------------|--------------------|-----------------|-------------|
| Base         | +8%              | 70%                | $1,240,000            | $320,000           | 6 (2 senior)    | 2           |
| Conservative | +4%              | 55%                | $980,000              | $420,000           | 4 (1 senior, 2 junior) | 4   |
| Aggressive   | +15%             | 80%                | $1,450,000            | $220,000           | 10 (3 senior)   | 1           |

Key metric outputs (first 3 months of horizon):
- Base: Token unit cost = $0.0018 per token (incl infra amortized), gross margin at current price = 41%.
- Conservative: Token unit cost = $0.00195 per token, gross margin = 36% (but lower fixed runway burn).
- Aggressive: Token unit cost = $0.00165 per token, gross margin = 44% (higher fixed commitments).

Role-swapbook constructs (novel suggestion):
- Swapbook A (conservative tilt): For every 1 senior infra hire deferred, hire 2 juniors + 0.6 contractor FTE for cross-team integration. Expected immediate OPEX drop of 12% vs senior hire, ramp to parity in 5–7 months.
- Swapbook B (capacity tilt): For each reserved GPU tranche reduced, allocate equivalent monthly $ to burst credits + contractor on-call. Reduces fixed cost exposure but raises per-GPU marginal cost.

Pricing sensitivity experiments (what we simulated):
- Price down 20%: demand boost in model = +18% (elasticity -0.9). Net effect: revenue -6% vs baseline, margin compression severe for Aggressive reserved heavy plan.
- Price up 10%: demand dips -7%, but per-token margin improves; reserved-heavy plan benefits.
- Trigger rules: if realized price compression >10% for two consecutive months, move to Conservative preset (cut reserved by 15%, increase burst cap).

Small numeric worked example (quick sanity calc):
- Baseline monthly tokens served: 320M tokens.
- Cost components: reserved infra $1.24M, burst $0.32M, infra-sre people & ops $0.45M, model licensing & misc $0.11M.
- Total cost = $2.12M => unit cost = $2.12M / 320M = $0.000006625 per token? (this is illustrative; check units vs per-token convention).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Revalidate GPU-hour pricing with cloud infra (list current vendor quotes; possible spot schedule).
- Confirm quality/regression multiplier for swapbook; ask Applied ML to run an eval on 5 eval prompt sets.
- Align quota and SLO changes with product teams before reducing reserved commits.

Recommendations (next 90 days):
1) Approve pilot: 1 swapbook squad (create 2 junior + 1 contractor vs 1 senior) for infra tuning; allocate $60k/month burst cushion.
2) Finance to model three-month cashflow sensitivity on price shock -12% and provide runway impact statement.
3) Create automated monitor: token price vs realized revenue margin; add Slack alert when 3-week rolling margin < target by 6 points.
4) Procurement to re-negotiate burst block discount with cloud partner (ask for 15% off on orders > $400k/mo).

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- Numbers are preliminary; many are rounded for readability.
- This doc intentionally mixes quick heuristics + explicit triggers so product/ops can act programmatically.
- If we like swapbook pilot results, consider codifying into hiring playbook (Finance + People Ops).

Appendix (quick comps):
- Break-even reserve utilization: roughly 62% of peak; below that, burst-heavy becomes cheaper on per-token basis after factoring flexibility cost.
- Candidate roles (title mapping): Senior Infra = "Infra Reliability Engineer (L5)", Junior = "Infra Engineer (L3)", Contractor = "ML Infra Contractor (short-term)".

End of sheet.

Author notes: Maya Chen - happy to walk through numbers live. This is intentionally a working artifact; please flag the rows you want expanded into a formal model.
